text:
sam.kim: hey folks — opened my first PR but hitting a few local setup quirks, can someone point me to the lightweight checklist for small patches?
kevin: congrats on the PR! link: https://redwood.dev/docs/pr-process — short version: small atomic commits, run linters/tests locally, add a short description with motivation.
sam.kim: thanks — two quick things: pre-commit keeps failing on `black` formatting even after running `make format`, and the test runner times out on `tests/integration/runtime` unless I set an env var. anyone seen this?
olivia: yep — if you're on mac/arm you need to install the binary wheels via `./scripts/setup-python.sh --for-dev` once. For black: we use pyproject.toml config; `poetry run black .` should match CI.
kevin: also we added a small caching step in the script. try `./scripts/bootstrap && ./scripts/ci-local.sh --cache` — that speeds up dependency installs.
sam.kim: for the integration timeout i get `RuntimeError: no GPU available` in the logs even though I have an NVIDIA box — maybe the tests assume a CUDA toolkit in PATH.
olivia: integration tests that touch the runtime require `CI_RUNTIME_GPU=1` to run locally, otherwise they get skipped in CI. We usually run them in a container: `docker compose -f docker/integration.yml up --build`.
sam.kim: perfect, will try. any rules about branch names and commit messages?
kevin: branch naming: `feature/<jira>-short-desc` or `fix/<area>-short-desc`. Commit messages follow Conventional Commits: `feat(runtime): add prefix caching` etc. Keep PRs < 400 LOC if possible.
sam.kim: who should I request for review on a infra/runtime change?
olivia: for runtime changes ping @kevin + @olivia and add `triage/runtime` label. For docs changes just ping `#devex` and add `docs` label.
sam.kim: CI started on my PR but ci-bot shows failures:
ci-bot: test-coverage failed: diff shows missing coverage in `inference/pipeline.py`
ci-bot: ```
FAIL tests/unit/test_pipeline.py::test_prefix_cache_invalidation - AssertionError: expected 1 but got 0
```
sam.kim: hmm I ran `pytest tests/unit -k pipeline` locally and it passed. CI log has `sqlite3.OperationalError: unable to open database file`.
kevin: that often means the temp DB path in the test uses a relative path that CI runs from. Use the fixture `tmp_path` or set `TEST_DB=/tmp/ci-test.db` in env while running locally to reproduce.
olivia: pro tip: run `make test-local` — it sets the env and runs the same test subset as CI. Also check pre-commit hooks with `pre-commit run --all-files` to catch linting issues before pushing.
sam.kim: ok will re-run with `TEST_DB` and `CI_RUNTIME_GPU`. Also noticed a small confusing bit in the contributing doc about when to rebase vs merge — can we clarify?
docs-bot: docs updated: /contributing.md clarified on rebase policy — small PRs: rebase; long-lived feature branches: merge with a squash commit. https://redwood.dev/docs/contributing (updated) :memo:
kevin: tiny PR best practice: keep the branch up to date before requesting review; prefer a single squashed commit for user-visible features, but keep sensible intermediate commits for complex refactors.
sam.kim: awesome, that helps. last question: are there size/perf checks I should be aware of?
olivia: CI runs `size-check` which looks for +10% regression in model binary assets and `perf-smoke` which runs a few synthetic invocations. If your changes touch model serialization or quantization, ping the perf-team early.
sam.kim: got it. thanks everyone! i'll push the fix and re-run CI. :rocket:
